prompt: What is the volume of a cylinder with radius $3$ and height $10$?
hint: Volume of a cylinder is the base area times the height.

hints.text: Volume of a cylinder is the base area times the height.
The base is a circle of area $\pi(3)^2 = 9\pi$.

learningObjective: Compute the volume of a cylinder.
explanation: Volume $= \pi r^2 h$, which is the circular base area times the height.
Choice A forgets to square the radius; choice D squares the height instead.

alternativeExplanations.title: Every prism and cylinder follows one rule
steps: Volume $=$ base area $\times$ height, whatever the base shape is.
For a cylinder the base is a circle; for a rectangular prism it is a rectangle.
Cones and pyramids take a third of that — the $\tfrac{1}{3}$ appears exactly when the shape narrows to a point.
